chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The freed slave is the mawla (client), and the child belongs to whomever he wishes."

key_terms.الْمَوْلَى: The mawla (client/patron), referring to the status of freedom and clientage
key_terms.يَنْتَمِي: Belongs/relates (in terms of lineage and inheritance)

ai.seo_question: Who does the child of a freed slave belong to in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'al-waladu li-l-mahdil' is applied specifically to the context of manumission, establishing that the child of a freed slave belongs to the freed person themselves rather than the former master. This ruling underscores the severance of the patron-client bond regarding lineage, ensuring that the offspring inherit the social and legal status of the mother or father who was freed, a principle crucial for determining inheritance shares in Shia jurisprudence. The hadith highlights the Imam's role in clarifying the practical implications of the 'mawla' status on family structure and property rights.
